title: Promising but missing critical features
body: Ssh-agent support (with agent forwarding) would be great. SSH jumphost/proxyconnect is a hard requirement for complex bastion setup. A MacOS version (with iCloud sync so I can sync my machine collection and snippets) would be cool.

title: Incompatible with herdr and fish
body: First, the app looks and feels great. It’s one I can tell I want to use, however when I try to connect to my host running Linux and default SHELL fish via Moshi and herdr , I get an un quoted string literal error, which terminates the connection. Any chance there is a fix for the client side script?

title: Maybe promising
body: Secure enclave key support is nice. Min font size of 10 is criminal (need to be able to go down to 3 and support pinch zoom for it, im trying to be productive here). Being able to define multitouch gestures is also much needed. No dedicated herdr gui, only TUI. The command button is 100% opaque and blocks content, which is ridiculous since it stays in the same place and easy to reach; great concept though. Updgradrd to 4 stars because whats been implemented is beautiful and robust, but cant be a 5 until i am able to wanna use it on a regular basis.

title: it’s super useful when i’m lazy and don’t want to get out of bed
body: the way this is designed is super useful. it's a little bit of a learning curve because you have to learn how to use this dial but it's probably a five-minute max learning curve to be honest. it's really helpful having the voice command to type in and then it automatically sends in there. i personally use wezterm plus herdr similar to kun chen’s actual setup and i've learned to actually love using this over mac terminals. it's like the best way to use terminals and so this is a better way than terminus which was the previous app i was using. it is far far easier to use. i think it still has some room for improvement. i'm not sure where yet. it could improve upon because it is a very difficult thing to squeeze all of your terminals into one app or into one little phone screen. i think notifications could be the next big thing here: getting notified on my phone when a terminal is finished working. wondering if that's possible

title: Ultimate Remote Terminal Tool
body: I’ve tried all the popular terminal apps for iOS and they all have shortcomings, mostly from how hard it is to interact with the keyboard and things like copy and paste. And it’s especially bad when you’re using coding agents like Claude, Codex, Grok or Pi with a tool like tmux or herdr. But SSHHIP’s floating action button which lets you pick and choose exactly what you need between the keyboard, pasteboard, voice input, herdr support, and snippets has made it my new daily driver for my iPad and iPhone when I need to check on my agents away from home.
